en:
Anyway, let's not stick around.
Wouldn't want Ed to show up with an army.
It's Date-san.
Kiryu. Where are you?

In Kamurocho. I'm over at
the Children's Park with Akiyama.

Got it. Think the two of you
could come by Touto Hospital?

I have some bad news. I'm not
sure of all the details yet...
But it's Haruka.
She's been in an accident in Kamurocho.
They're not sure if she'll pull through.
Hold on a second!
Haruka was in Kamurocho?
What?

I'll fill you in once you're here.
Hurry.
Hey, hold on! Kiryu-san!
Kiryu!
Date-san!
Excuse me, are you a patient here?
Well, uh...

If not, I must ask you to leave.
Your hygiene is a health hazard!
This is one of my coworkers on the force.

He's the one who let me know
about Haruka's accident.

The name's Honjo. Date-san's told
me a great deal about you.

What about Haruka?
Where is she!?

In the ICU. She's in no state
to be accepting visitors.

She fractured both her hip and shoulder,
but the cranial damage is life threatening.

She's in critical condition,
unconscious at the moment.
Wh-What happened?
It was a hit-and-run.

Some reckless punk drove into her.
The culprit's still at large.
A hit-and-run...
Are you okay, Kiryu?
No. I can barely think straight.
I can imagine.
But there's another piece to the puzzle.
What do you mean?

Come with me.
I need to show you something.
Just over there.

Haruka was clutching someone tight
when she saw the car coming.

A life she wanted to protect,
even if it meant risking her own.
What!?
This child...
...is Haruka's?
I don't believe it.

Well, it's time to start.
Look at his name.
It's Haruto.
There's no doubt, he's Haruka's kid.

No way...
You're sure!?
The last name's just icing on the cake.
Haruka would've died to keep him safe.
That's only a mother's sacrifice.
<font_kind=yakuza_italic>Haruto Sawamura</font_kind>

It's an honor to have you here,
Fourth Chairman.

Good afternoon. I'm Someya,
Patriarch of the Someya Family.

Your recent stint in jail was very
much appreciated. You did well.
So you knew I'd come back?

You'll have to forgive the actions of
my subordinate, Fourth Chairman.
He's caused a misunderstanding.
And what exactly do you mean by that?

Let's table that conversation for now.
Perhaps we can discuss further inside?

I'm sure your time behind bars has
left you exhausted, and besides...

Sugai-san has been looking forward
to meeting you.
You know of Sugai-san, yes?

His Tojo history may be longer than
yours, Kiryu-san.

With the sixth chairman indisposed for
his trial, Sugai-san is acting chairman.

And he's the one who had
that guy trailing me?
Again, let's talk inside.

I would love to be regaled by the tales
of your days as a young yakuza, Fourth Chairman.

I'm sure we could all stand to learn a thing
or two from a man as accomplished as you.
Right?

Excuse me.
Apologies for the intrusion.
Come in.
I've brought the fourth chairman.
Long time no see, Fourth Chairman.
Do you remember me?
It appears the answer is no...

Well, I've only ever been an advisor,
even under the sixth chairman's rule.
I don't blame you.

As I'm sure you heard, they called on me
to step in after the sixth chairman's arrest.

Just as the Tojo Clan was getting younger,
the old guard swoops in to fix things.
We must seem rather unstable in your eyes.
This is quite a table you brought in here.

Yakuza seem to talk more with
our pens than our fists these days.
Another sign of the times.

And Someya over there? He doesn't
look like much of a paper pusher to me.
I leave the math to the number crunchers.
Every yakuza has his role to play, you know.
Please. Take a seat, Fourth Chairman.
I don't plan on staying long.

But before I go,
I do have a few questions.

I assume this is about the hit-and-run
on your sweet Haruka?

What a terrible tragedy.
You have my condolences.

When did you hear about Haruka's
accident? Who told you?

I was informed by the police
not long after the incident.

Do they tell you everything
that happens in Kamurocho?

It's no secret that Haruka Sawamura is
very special to you, Fourth Chairman.

Naturally, that significance is what led
the police to contact us so quickly.
Did you have any other questions for me?

At the scene of the accident,
there was a man spying on me with a camera.
He said he was with the Someya Family.
Did you give that order, Sugai?

It wasn't spying.
It was protection.

We've been looking for you ever since
we heard you'd returned to Kamurocho.

Checking in on you at the scene of the accident
was the only way to confirm your well-being.
Someya speaks the truth.
I honestly thought it a bit extreme.
But we're at war with the Chinese, you know.

Though you're a civilian now, they may not
have extended you a civilian's courtesy.
I didn't ask for that.
And I don't need your help.

You're a man of strong character,
Fourth Chairman. I'm well aware of that.

Hence why I chose to act in secret.
You would never knowingly accept our help.
My apologies if I've upset you.

Didn't I tell you, Sugai-san? The fourth
chairman doesn't need our protection.

It'd be pointless for the Chinese
to target him anyway.
The Dragon of Dojima is dead.
Any weight that name carried is gone.

We may have been watching you, yes...
But don't assume you have any value to us.

The current conflict rests on
my generation, not yours.
It has nothing to do with a fossil like you.
The new generation sounds pretty cocky.

This war with the Chinese
has left us no choice.
And is it any wonder?

Until recently, the yakuza's power
was vested in its financial prowess.

So it follows that the sixth chairman's
officers were all very intelligent men.
But, now things have changed.

With the Tojo Clan at war, all that matters
now is whether or not a yakuza can fight.

Your value as a yakuza has a direct
correlation to your body count.

In other words, you ascend by force.
It's the dawn of a new era for us yakuza.

Doesn't that sound amazing,
Fourth Chairman?

You rose to power in much the same way,
didn't you?

Now even the once invincible Sugai-san
has to rely on youth to keep the clan intact.
Isn't that right, Sugai-san?

They risk their lives for our cause,
so we promote them. It's only fair.

I didn't come here today to talk
about the value of a yakuza.
I'm only going to ask this once.

Were you involved in Haruka's accident?
You really know nothing?

What are you implying? What purpose
would such a horrible act even serve?
As it stands, I believe you.

Haruka and I have less than
nothing to do with your little war.
But hear me now...

If the Tojo Clan even <font_kind=yakuza_italic>thinks</font_kind>
about laying a hand on my family...
...I will bury all of you.

We aren't interested in making
an enemy of the Dragon of Dojima.

We have plenty of other playthings
to keep us occupied.
Let's not do this, Kiryu-san.

And let Nojiri take him? He doesn't
care what happens to these kids.

The only one who can keep this
baby safe... is me.

Maybe, but the guy did have
<font_kind=yakuza_italic>some</font_kind> logic behind him.

People who know you personally are
one thing, but to the rest of the world...
...You're just an ex-con of a yakuza.

I'm sorry. But there's not much we can do
for the kid until Haruka-chan wakes up.

We have to let the authorities
handle this how they see fit.

What if Haruka takes a turn for the worse?
Her son would...

What are you saying, Kiryu-san?
Don't even go down that path!
How can you know?
They'd put Haruto in an orphanage for sure.

And if they did, there'd be nothing I could
do to help him. We'd be total strangers.
I'd never see his face again.

That's what happens when a child
gets sent off to an orphanage like that.

No matter how hard I struggle,
it'll be impossible for me to help him.

Haruka wouldn't want that
for her only child.

You see?
This is my only chance.

What are you doing in here?
Get your hands off that child!

We're in the middle of something here.
Can you wait outside?
Absolutely not!

Unhand that child this instant!
You think you can get away with this!?
I'm taking him with me.

I'll give him back once Haruka wakes up.
Trust me.
I can't let you do this, Kiryu-san.

You'd get taken back in, this time as
a kidnapper. How could I face Haruka?
You'd really do that to her?

My choice is made, Akiyama!
You can't change my mind.
I'm trying anyway, Kiryu-san.

I'm telling you you're making
the wrong call here.

For once in your life, think something through!
You've gotta consider the consequences!
Enough!
You think I don't know this is wrong?

Whatever happens to me doesn't matter,
and nobody else does either.
I need to protect Haruka's son, now.
I have to do this.
Kiryu-san!
If you're dead-set on stopping me...
...There's only one way forward.
Step aside.
Akiyama!
Dammit, why won't you listen!?

Just a little longer, okay?
You must be starving, huh?

You not <font_kind=yakuza_italic>seriously</font_kind> giving
that to a baby, are you?

If it's food you're looking for,
try something more like this.
You never change, do you?
Still a loose cannon.

What happened?
What's going on with her?

She had to have emergency surgery.
They managed to save her life...
...But she's still comatose.

The doctors don't know when
she'll regain consciousness. Or if.
How did it come to this?

Hey, you went poking your nose
around Kamurocho today, right?

You learn anything about what
happened after Haruka disappeared?
Nothing at all.

She left Okinawa, disappeared for
three years, then showed up here.
That's all I know.
I see.

In that case, this is probably
the only lead we have.
Hm? What's that?
A photo we pulled from Haruka's cell data.

We managed to recover it even though
the phone got smashed in the accident.
Any idea where it was taken?
This background tells me nothing.

Well, we actually managed to pull
GPS data from the photo too.

These crazy phones record the
exact spot a picture was taken in.
And that spot is, well...
It's in Hiroshima.
Hiroshima?

Yeah, somewhere around Jingaicho,
in the city of Onomichi.

You're telling me Haruka left
Okinawa to go to Hiroshima?
Not so bad, huh?
Don't you think, Haruto?
Oh?

Is that an accident I smell?
Hold on a second.

Hey, no squirming.
I'll be done soon.
Whoa!
I'm not falling for that one again.
Are you hungry?

Uh oh...
I'm all out of milk.

Haruto.
Here, I got you some milk.
Sorry it took so long.

What's wrong?
Isn't this what you wanted!?

Kiryu-san?
It's Kiyomi, from Snack Kiyomi.
O-Oh. It's open!
Come on in!
Ah, figures.
Can I hold him?

This little guy's not hungry at all.
Just sleepy.
Sleepy!?

Best thing to do now is hold
him close and wait a while.
That's it...?
You!
Surprised t'see ya still here.
Let me guess... Nagumo?
What do you want?
Y'don't gotta be so cold.
We ain't strangers no more. Right?
I see you brought friends.

Why are you gunning for me like this?
I don't want any trouble.

Then maybe y'should run on back to Tokyo.
How 'bout that?

Y'know this guy, Cap?
Who is he?
A mighty fine question!

Y'wanna know who he is?
A filthy outsider from Tokyo!

Look at 'im! Don't that ugly mug
jus' make ya wanna cry?
Um, Cap...
We should probably get going.

We're gonna get chewed out again
if we're not there soon.
Ya turdbrain!
Ow!
Ain't nobody gon' chew us out!

Y'hear, Yuta!? Don't go talkin' to
yer captain like that again!
I'm in the middle of somethin' here!

It looks like yer target's
not interested. See?
That highfalutin' asshole!
Let's deal with him later, yeah?
We can't start without ya there, Cap.
Yer in luck this time, Kiryu!

But listen, y'ain't gon' survive our
next meetin'! Remember that!
What a mess.
That guy just won't leave me alone...

I thought Nagumo was supposed
to take baseball seriously.

He usually does, but today he's
really out for blood.

C'mon! Y'hurtin'?
Don't y'wanna fight me, Ino!?
Let's dance!
What're y'doin', ya coward!?

Y'think yer too cool to throw down, huh!?
Hey, I didn't realize yer balls fell off!

Y'know the next batter?
It's that Kiryu guy.

Right. Why's Cap been gettin' all
worked up over him anyways?

He's screwed if he can't focus on the game.
Baseball's his one savin' grace.

It doesn't really matter why. He's just
not gonna be happy 'til he fights someone.

Let's get this over with so we
can go home in peace.
Good thinkin'.
You sure, Kiryu-san?
I'm the one Nagumo wants.

If I'd gone up to bat earlier,
nobody else would've had to get hurt.
So my prey's finally showed up.

Y'know, my grip's been
slippin' real bad today.
